# java-guardrails 0.3.1

Maven measurements and planted-violation proofs now build sibling dependencies from the working
reactor. Scoped commands use `-am` and a clean lifecycle; source-only check goals compile reactor
prerequisites first. No preliminary install into a shared local repository is required.

A shared build policy enables the kit's Error Prone profile only for Error Prone and NullAway,
and skips unrelated kit gates for every measurement and proof. The requested gate's own disable
settings remain authoritative: negative controls must still reject a disabled gate.

Module inventory follows declared reactor membership, including Maven-resolved profile modules,
rather than selecting every source directory under the repository. Standalone nested tools no
longer cause a root `-pl` failure. Maven errors remain visible when a build fails before tests.

`EXCLUDED_MODULES: path, other/path` is now independent of `TEST_SUPPORT_MODULES`. Existing
`TEST_SUPPORT_MODULES: exclude ...` entries continue to exclude those paths. An exclusion that
names only a non-test module no longer suppresses the test-support decision; record that decision
when PMD emits it. No target file is migrated automatically.

Excluded modules may still be upstream build prerequisites. Their tests and the requested gate
may run, and a failure stops measurement or proof. External artifacts still use Maven settings;
this change does not isolate arbitrary external SNAPSHOT dependencies. The conventional
`src/main/java` layout within the target remains the inventory contract.
